A young (26 yo) woman developed sudden sharp low back pain during exercise with pain radiating down the side of one leg into the foot — a classic radicular distribution (likely L5 or S1 root). Examination shows localized lumbar tenderness, limited ROM from pain, and a reportedly positive straight-leg-raise (a sensitive test for nerve-root irritation), while reflexes, motor strength and sensation can remain normal early in acute radiculopathy, explaining the otherwise normal neuro exam. Documentation conflicts about exact laterality and SLR degrees do not negate the overall pattern. Acute muscle strain or sacroiliac/piriformis pain are less likely to produce true radiating pain into the foot and a positive SLR. No signs of cauda equina (bowel/bladder dysfunction) are present.

[DIAGNOSIS] Acute lumbar disc herniation causing lumbar radiculopathy (sciatica), most likely affecting the L5–S1 nerve root.
